verdict.rationale: RudderStack's own docs describe an "open source version" that runs as a standalone data plane and control plane on PostgreSQL, so its source is publicly readable. Community threads say the license moved from SSPL to AGPLv3 and then to the Elastic License. The Elastic License is source-available rather than OSI-open, so whether the current license counts as "open" is uncertain. missing for 10: a first-party statement of the current license, a link to the source repository, and clarity on which components are covered by an OSI-approved license.
